text: SYSTEM DESIGN
The Complete Zero-to-Interview-Ready Roadmap
100% Free Resources · Official Docs · Curated YouTube Playlists
Companion document: System Design — Top Interview & Hackathon
Questions with Answers
How to use this roadmap

This roadmap is organized as 13 chapters, from absolute fundamentals to advanced distributed-systems
theory and real case studies. Go top to bottom in order the first time. Every topic below links to a genuinely
free resource — an official doc, a free YouTube video/playlist, or a free open-source repo. Nothing here
requires a paid course or subscription. Spend 60–90 minutes/day; most people finish the core roadmap (Ch.
1–9) in 5–7 weeks, then spend 2–3 weeks purely on case studies and mock interviews.

Suggested pace:
•
Week 1–2: Chapters 1–3 (Foundations, Networking, Core Concepts)
•
Week 3–4: Chapters 4–6 (Databases, Caching, Messaging)
•
Week 5: Chapters 7–9 (Scalability patterns, Consistency/Consensus, Microservices)
•
Week 6: Chapters 10–12 (Security, Observability, Storage)
•
Week 7 onward: Chapter 13 case studies + mock interviews using the companion Q&A; PDF
CHAPTER 1  |  Foundations Before System Design

Skip this chapter only if you're already comfortable with how computers talk to each other over a network and
basic OS concepts.
1.1 How the Internet works
IP addressing, routers, packets, and how a request physically travels from your laptop to a server.
I How the Internet Works (freeCodeCamp) — https://www.youtube.com/@freecodecamp
Search their channel for 'How the Internet Works' — full free video.

I MDN: How the Web works —
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/Getting_started_with_the_web/How_the_Web_works
1.2 OSI Model & TCP/IP stack
The 7 layers, and practically, the 4-layer TCP/IP model used in real systems.

I OSI Model Explained —
https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ddos/glossary/open-systems-interconnection-model-osi/

I Gaurav Sen — System Design Playlist —
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX
Watch the early videos on networking basics + system design primer.
1.3 TCP vs UDP
Reliable ordered delivery (TCP) vs fast connectionless delivery (UDP) — and when each is used.
I TCP vs UDP (Hussein Nasser) — https://www.youtube.com/@hnasr
1.4 DNS resolution & HTTP/HTTPS basics
How a domain name becomes an IP address; request/response cycle; TLS handshake basics.
I DNS: How it works — Cloudflare Learning Center — https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/what-is-dns/
I MDN: An overview of HTTP — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Overview
1.5 Client-server architecture & OS basics
Processes vs threads, concurrency vs parallelism, memory basics — enough OS to reason about servers.
I roadmap.sh — System Design Roadmap — https://roadmap.sh/system-design
The visual, interactive master roadmap this document expands on.
CHAPTER 2  |  Core Concepts & Vocabulary
These are the words interviewers expect you to use precisely.
2.1 Scalability — Vertical vs Horizontal
Scaling up (bigger machine) vs scaling out (more machines) and their trade-offs.

I Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling — Gaurav Sen —
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX
2.2 Latency vs Throughput vs Bandwidth
Time-per-request vs requests-per-second vs max data-per-second — and why optimizing one can hurt another.
I ByteByteGo — YouTube Channel — https://www.youtube.com/@ByteByteGo
Short, visual explainer videos on nearly every core term.
2.3 Availability, Reliability & Fault Tolerance
'Nines' of availability (99.9% vs 99.99%), redundancy, failover, graceful degradation.
I Google SRE Book — Availability chapters (free) — https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/
2.4 CAP Theorem & PACELC
Why you can't have Consistency + Availability + Partition tolerance all at once, and what PACELC adds.

I CAP Theorem — Gaurav Sen —
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX
I Martin Kleppmann's talks & papers (free) — https://martin.kleppmann.com/
Author of 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications' — free talks/slides on his site.
2.5 Consistency Models
Strong, eventual, causal, and read-your-writes consistency — where each is used in practice.
I InterviewReady — Arpit Bhayani (YouTube) — https://www.youtube.com/@AsliEngineering
Deep, engineering-heavy explanations of consistency & distributed systems.

CHAPTER 4  |  Databases
4.1 SQL vs NoSQL
Schema-rigid relational databases vs flexible-schema stores; when to pick which.
I system-design-primer (GitHub, free & open source) — https://github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer
The most-starred free system design repo on GitHub — read the SQL vs NoSQL section.
4.2 Indexing
B-Trees, hash indexes, composite indexes — how databases avoid full table scans.
I Use The Index, Luke! (free SQL indexing guide) — https://use-the-index-luke.com/
4.3 Normalization vs Denormalization
Reducing redundancy vs optimizing for read speed at the cost of duplication.

I PostgreSQL official docs — Normalization basics —
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-table.html
4.4 Replication (Leader-Follower, Multi-Leader, Leaderless)
Copying data across nodes for availability and read scaling; sync vs async replication.
I PostgreSQL — Replication docs (official) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/high-availability.html
4.5 Sharding & Partitioning
Splitting data by key range/hash across nodes; the hot-shard problem and how to avoid it.
I MongoDB Docs — Sharding (official) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/

I Consistent Hashing explained — Tech Dummies (YouTube) —
https://www.youtube.com/@TechDummiesNarendraL

text: CHAPTER 5  |  Caching
5.1 Why & where to cache
Client cache, CDN cache, application cache, database cache — the caching hierarchy.
I Caching best practices — AWS official docs — https://aws.amazon.com/caching/best-practices/
5.2 Cache Strategies
Cache-aside, write-through, write-back, and read-through — with their failure modes.
I Caching strategies — AWS Database Blog (official) — https://aws.amazon.com/caching/database-caching/
5.3 Eviction Policies
LRU, LFU, FIFO — how caches decide what to throw away when full.
I Redis docs — Eviction policies (official) — https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/eviction/
5.4 Redis & Memcached in practice
I Redis University (100% free official courses) — https://redis.io/university/

6.1 Message Queues vs Pub/Sub
Point-to-point delivery (queue) vs fan-out delivery to many subscribers (pub/sub).
I RabbitMQ official tutorials (free) — https://www.rabbitmq.com/tutorials
6.2 Apache Kafka fundamentals
Topics, partitions, consumer groups, offsets — the backbone of most event-driven systems.
I Apache Kafka official documentation — https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/

I Kafka Explained — Gaurav Sen —
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX

Producers/consumers, event sourcing, and decoupling services through events instead of direct calls.

I Microsoft Azure Architecture Center — Event-driven architecture (official) —
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/guide/architecture-styles/event-driven
CHAPTER 7  |  Scalability Patterns
7.1 Rate Limiting
Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed/sliding window — protecting systems from overload/abuse.
I System Design: Rate Limiter — ByteByteGo (YouTube) — https://www.youtube.com/@ByteByteGo
7.2 Consistent Hashing
Distributing keys across nodes so adding/removing a node reshuffles minimal data.

I Consistent Hashing — Gaurav Sen —
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX
7.3 Database Scaling Patterns
Read replicas, connection pooling, CQRS (separating read/write models).

I Microsoft Architecture Center — CQRS pattern (official) —
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/cqrs
7.4 Bloom Filters, Heartbeats & Health Checks

https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/tag/bloom-filters/
CHAPTER 8  |  Distributed Systems Theory
8.1 Consensus Algorithms — Paxos & Raft
How distributed nodes agree on a single value/leader despite failures.
I The Raft Consensus Algorithm (official site, free, interactive) — https://raft.github.io/
I MIT 6.824 — Distributed Systems (free full course, lectures + labs) — https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/6.824/
One of the best free graduate-level distributed systems courses on the internet.
8.2 Distributed Transactions — 2PC & Saga Pattern
Two-phase commit for atomicity across services vs the Saga pattern for long-running workflows.

I Microsoft Architecture Center — Saga pattern (official) —
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/saga
8.3 Vector Clocks, Quorums & Idempotency
Ordering events without a global clock; read/write quorums (R+W>N); making retried requests safe.
I InterviewReady — Arpit Bhayani (YouTube) — https://www.youtube.com/@AsliEngineering

system-design-primer (GitHub) — the single best free repo; has flashcards, case studies, and

MIT 6.824 Distributed Systems (free course) — the gold standard for going deep on distributed systems
theory.

Asli Engineering / InterviewReady — Arpit Bhayani (YouTube) — engineering-first, no-fluff explanations.

AWS Architecture Center (official) and Azure Architecture Center (official) — real reference architectures
